review.summary: The analytics feature adds several security-relevant defects: an admin JWT is written to logs on every view request, the visitor key is taken from the request body (dedup bypass / analytics poisoning), CSV export is vulnerable to formula injection, the new public view endpoint has no rate limit, and the top-viewed search builds a raw regex from user input. At least one CRITICAL finding, so changes are requested.

findings.title: Admin JWT written to logs on every view request
findings.rationale: `console.log('[analytics] auth header:', req.headers.authorization)` logs the full `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header. Attacker input: any request to `POST /api/blog/:blogId/view` carrying an Authorization header (or an admin simply opening a public blog post while logged in). Achieves: the admin JWT is persisted in server/aggregator logs; anyone with log read access can replay it for full admin access. Violates AC-10.2 (authorization headers/tokens shall never be written to logs).
findings.suggestion: Remove the console.log entirely; if diagnostics are needed, log only a boolean such as `isAdminView` or a truncated hash, never the header value.

findings.title: CSV export is vulnerable to spreadsheet formula injection
findings.rationale: `escapeCSV` only quotes cells containing `,`, `"` or newline; it never prefixes cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`. Attacker input: a blog title/category such as `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","x")` or `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0` (title is user-controlled via the blog create/edit flow). Achieves: when an admin exports the CSV and opens it in Excel/Sheets, the cell is evaluated as a formula, enabling data exfiltration or command execution. AC-5.6 explicitly requires prefixing such cells with a single quote.
findings.suggestion: In `escapeCSV`, after stringifying, if the first character is `=`, `+`, `-` or `@`, prefix with `'` before applying quote/escape handling.

findings.title: Visitor key is taken from the request body, bypassing deduplication
findings.rationale: `const visitorKey = req.body?.visitorKey` lets the client choose the dedup key. Attacker input: repeated `POST /api/blog/:blogId/view` calls each with a fresh random `visitorKey`. Achieves: the 24h dedup check never matches, so view counts are inflated arbitrarily and analytics are poisoned; it also allows unbounded document creation. AC-6.3 requires the key to be derived on the server (`sha256(ip + user-agent)` or `sha256(X-Visitor-ID)`), and the body shall not be able to set it. Note the server-side `computeVisitorKey` in `server/src/utils/viewTracking.js` already exists but is not used here.
findings.suggestion: Ignore `req.body.visitorKey`; derive the key server-side via `computeVisitorKey(req)` (or equivalent) and use that for the dedup lookup and document creation.

findings.title: Public view endpoint has no rate limit
findings.rationale: `blogRouter.post('/:blogId/view', recordView)` is unauthenticated and has no limiter, unlike the adjacent comment/generate routes. Attacker input: a high-volume stream of unauthenticated POSTs to `/api/blog/:blogId/view`. Achieves: each request performs a DB lookup and write, enabling write flooding/DoS and view-count inflation. AC-6.7 requires a dedicated 30 requests/minute per-IP limit on this endpoint.
findings.suggestion: Add a dedicated `viewLimiter` (30 req/min per IP) to the route, e.g. `blogRouter.post('/:blogId/view', viewLimiter, recordView)`.

findings.title: User-supplied regex in top-viewed search enables ReDoS / regex injection
findings.rationale: `blogFilter.title = { $regex: req.query.search, $options: 'i' }` passes the raw query string into a MongoDB regex without escaping or validation (`validateAnalyticsQuery` does not check `search`). Attacker input: `?search=(a+)+$` or `?search=.*`. Achieves: catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) against the database and arbitrary regex matching; free-text search is also explicitly out of scope per spec §11.
findings.suggestion: Escape the input (e.g. `escapeRegExp(req.query.search)`) and bound its length, or remove the search branch since search is out of scope for this PR.
